newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia business pleads for tough anti-drug law.
newsitem.headline: Colombia business pleads for tough anti-drug law.

text.p: Colombia's most powerful business leaders on Wednesday sent a plea to lawmakers to rescue tough anti-drug legislation now being considered by congress.

The call from the heads of three of the country's largest industrial and financial conglomerates came a day after lawmakers watered down a key provision of a bill designed to give the government powers to seize the assets of drug lords and their accomplices.
Colombia is under strong pressure from the United States to crack down on the country's drug cartels.

The letter to congress was signed by Carlos Ardila, who heads an industrial conglomerate of 30 companies, Augusto Lopez, chairman of brewer Bavaria, and Luis Carlos Sarmiento, a leading Colombian banker.

"In our role as Colombian entrepreneurs, justifiably worried about the fate of the country, we want to make a fervent and patriotic call for you to take part in discussions and votes to approve the text of the relevant article as it was approved by the Senate," the letter said.

The main body of the asset forfeiture law has passed both houses of congress but the Chamber of Representatives took the teeth out of the bill Tuesday night by voting down the proposal to seize drug-related assets accumulated over the last 20 years.

President Ernesto Samper's government was looking to open the way for a fresh vote on that clause. In its current form, the bill would only allow the confiscation of ill-gotten gains amassed after 1991.
